Radius scans locate the known Vicsek interaction radius and recover an independently specified clustering scale in experimental active rods. Local scale covariance yields the relation, while a tent map counterexample shows when reducing the stationary balance at each parent size to one moment fails.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to link cluster dynamics (merging/splitting) to static scaling via tracking conserved constituents, with applications to coupled map networks, coagulation-fragmentation, and Vicsek systems.
motivation: Clusters that merge and split lack a unique genealogy, making it challenging to connect dynamic behavior to static scaling properties.
method: Define a measure based on the host size of a conserved constituent and analyze across coupled map networks, coagulation-fragmentation dynamics, and Vicsek systems, using local scale covariance to derive the scaling relation.
result: The measure connects dynamic cluster statistics to static scaling without fitting, successfully recovering interaction radii in Vicsek systems and clustering scales in active rods, but fails under a tent map when stationary balance is reduced to a single moment.
conclusion: Provides a robust relationship between cluster dynamics and static scaling under certain conditions, though limitations highlight when simplified moment reductions are inadequate.

title: Computational Algorithms For Invariant Reduction Of Variational Forms
authors: Alexey Shevyakov Kostya Druzhkov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry reductions of partial differential equations (PDEs) inherit more geometric structures than other types of reductions: invariant conservation laws, variational structures, and, under suitable conditions, Hamiltonian-type structures of the original model descend to the reduced model through the mechanism of invariant reduction. This paper develops computational algorithms that carry out such reductions explicitly. We use the interpretation of variational [MATH]-forms as conservation laws of an enlarged system --- the (degree-shifted) tangent system --- consisting of the original equations together with their linearizations, in which the perturbation variables are treated as anticommuting. This allows us to formulate the algorithms using well-known concepts from the theory of conservation laws, naturally adapted to the graded-commutative setting. The reduction of conservation laws, variational [MATH]-forms, and presymplectic structures thereby becomes a single algorithmic procedure. We present (i) a homotopy-based reduction algorithm for systems of evolution equations, implemented in Maple; (ii) a descent reduction algorithm applicable to general [MATH]-normal systems for [MATH]; and (iii) a simple reduction algorithm available for point symmetries under suitable conditions, including the description of reductions in terms of systems involving fewer independent variables. Examples include nonlinear evolution equations in one and two spatial dimensions, the Laplace equation, the incompressible Euler equations, and the cotangent system of Pavlov's equation.
tldr: This paper develops computational algorithms for invariant reduction of variational forms in PDEs, preserving geometric structures like conservation laws and variational principles.
motivation: Symmetry reductions of PDEs often inherit geometric structures, but explicit computational methods for such reductions are lacking.
method: The authors interpret variational forms as conservation laws of a degree-shifted tangent system with anticommuting variables, and present three reduction algorithms (homotopy-based, descent, and point-symmetry based) implemented in Maple.
result: Algorithms are demonstrated on several PDEs, including nonlinear evolution equations, Laplace equation, incompressible Euler equations, and Pavlov's equation.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms provide a unified, computational approach to invariant reduction, extending existing theory to practical implementation.

title: Discretization-Aware Fine-Tuning For Quantum Machine Learning With Chemical Foundation Models
authors: Sonika Johri Shunji Matsuura
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A key challenge in practical quantum machine learning (QML), particularly for discriminative tasks such as classification, is the limited capacity of near-term quantum devices to encode high-dimensional classical data into small quantum registers. In optimized basis-encoded (bit-bit) settings, this constraint leads to cross-class collisions, where samples with different labels are mapped to the same discrete bit-string and thus become indistinguishable to any downstream model. In this work, we investigate how data representation affects QML performance under such severe information bottlenecks. We introduce discretization-aware fine-tuning (DAFT), a method that adapts a pre-trained chemical foundation model to produce representations that remain informative after quantization. DAFT reduces collision probability through a differentiable soft collision loss. We evaluate both quantum and classical models under a controlled setting in which they receive identical discretized bit-string inputs, isolating the effect of representation from model architecture. On the blood-brain barrier penetration (BBBP) molecular property prediction benchmark using ChemBERTa-77M, DAFT reduces collision counts by several orders of magnitude and improves quantum classification accuracy by more than 12 percentage points compared to a frozen backbone. Importantly, without DAFT, classical models outperform QML under the same input constraints. With DAFT, however, this comparison reverses at higher qubit counts. At 10 qubits, the quantum model surpasses a matched classical baseline trained on identical bit-strings (0.883 vs. 0.855, [MATH]). These results show that, in information-constrained regimes, achieving a quantum advantage critically depends on aligning continuous representations with discrete quantum encodings.
tldr: Introduces discretization-aware fine-tuning to reduce collision in quantum machine learning for molecular property prediction, showing quantum advantage at higher qubits.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited capacity to encode high-dimensional data, causing cross-class collisions in basis-encoded QML.
method: DAFT adapts a pre-trained chemical foundation model with a soft collision loss to produce representations that remain informative after discretization.
result: On BBBP, DAFT reduces collisions and improves quantum accuracy by 12+ points; comparisons reverse at 10 qubits.
conclusion: In information-constrained regimes, aligning continuous representations with quantum encodings is critical for quantum advantage.

title: Optimal Bounds For Embedded Eigenvalues Of One-dimensional Discrete Schr\"odinger Operators With Decaying Potentials
authors: Jifeng Chu, Wencai Liu, Kang Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operators Hu(n)=(\Delta+V)u(n)\nonumber on [MATH] with a self-adjoint boundary condition at [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the discrete Laplacian and [MATH] is a real-valued perturbation satisfying $[MATH]$ We determine the sharp transition for the asymptotic coefficient of \(V\) governing the existence and nonexistence of embedded eigenvalues.
tldr: This paper studies optimal bounds for embedded eigenvalues of one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operators with decaying potentials, focusing on spectral theory.
motivation: To understand the sharp conditions under which embedded eigenvalues exist for such operators, which is a fundamental question in spectral theory.
method: The authors employ analytical methods for one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operators, likely using asymptotic analysis and perturbation arguments.
result: They determine the sharp transition for the asymptotic coefficient of the potential that governs the existence and nonexistence of embedded eigenvalues.
conclusion: The paper provides optimal bounds for the appearance of embedded eigenvalues, contributing to the mathematical understanding of discrete Schrödinger operators.

title: Nodal Obstruction To Conditioned-diffusion Representations Of The Weak Momentum
authors: Chon-Fai Kam (universit\`a Degli Studi Di Palermo, Inserm BIGR U1134, Universit\'e Paris Cit\'e), Kai-Wen Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Schr\"odinger bridge constructions establish the existence of a conditioned process under a positivity hypothesis on the endpoint data, and three independent ones adopt it. We show that hypothesis fails on a definite locus once the conditioned object is the two-state amplitude [MATH] of a pre- and post-selected pair on configuration space, and that the failure is testable on recorded data. Whenever [MATH] has a moving zero of order [MATH] across which probability flows, no diffusion of constant diffusion coefficient can both carry the conditioned density and avoid the nodal curve: the current velocity it would need grows as the inverse [MATH]-th power of the distance to that curve and points toward it on one side, placing the curve at finite scale distance, so it is reached and not merely approached. Identifying the weak momentum with a bridge drift fails independently: for a free particle post-selected in position the current velocity is exactly minus the drift of the bridge to the target. The positive Doob [MATH]-transform and the Bernstein conditioning built on it exist wherever [MATH] is nodeless and fail on the nodal curve. There the osmotic part of the weak momentum diverges as the inverse distance to the zero and changes sign across it with a coefficient set by [MATH], while the current part stays bounded; that boundedness rests on the signed factorization of the real-envelope class and hides the obstruction from any picture built on the current velocity alone. A measured fringe visibility fixes a single length, which puts a Lorentzian of order [MATH] into the current channel reconstructed in the two-slit trajectory experiment if the contrast is limited by an off-axis zero, and nothing there if by incoherence. The results are one-dimensional, covering the separable transverse field of a two-slit geometry, not general two-dimensional vortices.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that a positivity hypothesis fails for conditioned-diffusion representations of the weak momentum, causing obstructions on nodal curves in certain quantum systems.
motivation: To establish conditioned-diffusion representations of weak momentum in quantum mechanics, specifically for pre- and post-selected two-state amplitudes on configuration space.
method: Mathematical analysis of quantum Schrödinger bridge constructions, examining the Doob h-transform and Bernstein conditioning where the amplitude is nodeless and identifying failure at nodal curves.
result: Shows that when the amplitude has a moving zero, no constant-coefficient diffusion can carry the conditioned density without crossing the nodal curve; the current velocity diverges, while the osmotic part diverges and the current part remains bounded, hiding the obstruction.
conclusion: There is a fundamental obstruction to representing weak momentum via conditioned diffusions in the presence of nodal curves, with testable consequences in two-slit experiments.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye, Yiqi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Being structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry [MATH] of order [MATH], photonic quasicrystals are capable to support stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry [MATH] of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states was not investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices were considered in this context. Here we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects -- disclinations -- introduced into their structure that allows to produce new quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We found two different classes of stable vortex solitons consisting of in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, while stability intervals for them broaden with decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry [MATH] of quasicrystal. Our results expand the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting new prospects for robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: The paper introduces disclinations into photonic quasicrystals to create new structures supporting stable vortex solitons.
motivation: To explore how discrete rotational symmetry affects vortex states in quasicrystals and to enable arbitrary symmetry orders via topological defects.
method: Global topological defects (disclinations) are added to Penrose tilings, generating quasicrystals with desired rotational symmetries, then linear and nonlinear vortex solutions are analyzed.
result: Two classes of stable vortex solitons with distinct intensity patterns are found, and low-charge solitons can be stable, with stability intervals broadening as symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The findings expand localization theory in quasicrystals and suggest new possibilities for robust optical information transmission.

title: A Silicon-Compatible Uncooled Compact Broadband Infrared Spectrometer
authors: A. Nomezine, G. Daligou, D. Vlassov, S. Assali, M. R. M. Atalla, O. Moutanabbir
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Infrared spectroscopy is a widely used technique for molecular identification, yet its widespread deployment remains constrained by bulky instrumentation, cryogenic cooling requirements, and limited portability. Here we demonstrate broadband near- to short-wave infrared spectroscopy enabled by a silicon-compatible GeSn photodetector integrated into a compact digital micromirror device-based single-pixel architecture. By combining detector design with targeted optical reconfiguration and wavelength recalibration, we extend the operational range up to 2.4 micrometers while maintaining room-temperature, zero-bias photovoltaic operation. System-level benchmarking quantifies the intrinsic trade-off between spectral extension and detectivity in narrow-bandgap photodetection, yielding a specific detectivity of [MATH] cm Hz[MATH] W[MATH] at 1.55 micrometers with an extended wavelength cut-off. We validate the capabilities of the obtained spectrometer through selective identification of representative commodity plastics, demonstrating a lightweight, low-power, and mechanically robust platform for portable and autonomous deployment. Despite the expected increase in generation-limited noise, access to strong polymer combination bands beyond 1.7 micrometers allows enhanced material discrimination. This work establishes a pathway toward scalable distributed molecular sensing and broadens access to infrared spectroscopy for environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and community-level chemical detection.
tldr: This paper presents a compact infrared spectrometer using a GeSn photodetector and single-pixel architecture, enabling room-temperature broadband spectroscopy for molecular identification, but it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum systems.
motivation: To overcome the bulkiness and cooling requirements of conventional infrared spectrometers, enabling portable and autonomous molecular sensing applications.
method: A silicon-compatible GeSn photodetector is integrated into a digital micromirror device-based single-pixel spectrometer, with optical reconfiguration and wavelength recalibration to extend the operational range.
result: The device operates up to 2.4 micrometers at room temperature, with specific detectivity at 1.55 micrometers, and successfully identifies representative commodity plastics, particularly using combination bands beyond 1.7 micrometers.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway toward scalable distributed infrared sensing but does not align with any of the four research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Large-Language Models As A Cognitive Virus
authors: Ricard Sol\'e, Giulio Ruffini, Francesca Castaldo, Marco Tuccio, Luis F. Seoane, Manlio de Domenico, Santiago F. Elena, David C. Krakauer, Michael Levin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. Here we propose that their diffusion can be understood through a viral analogy, with LLM use spreading through populations, becoming embedded in cognitive and cultural practices. We model transitions among uncoupled, coupled, and persistently dependent users, and show that the interplay between social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement can generate tipping points and technological lock-in. A central consequence is the possibility of runaway dynamics: once a critical threshold is crossed, small increases in adoption can trigger rapid population-level shifts toward persistent dependence, with abrupt losses in cognitive competence. The same framework, however, identifies conditions for cognitive immunization, based on reducing transmission and facilitating reversibility. Our results highlight how LLM adoption may involve nonlinear collective transitions with important consequences for cognitive autonomy.
tldr: This paper models the adoption of large language models as a viral process, demonstrating potential tipping points and lock-in effects leading to persistent dependence, while also identifying conditions for cognitive immunization.
motivation: To understand the societal and cognitive impact of LLM proliferation using concepts from epidemiology and nonlinear dynamics, highlighting risks of abrupt competence loss and collective transitions.
method: The study constructs a dynamical model with user states (uncoupled, coupled, persistently dependent), incorporating social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement, and analyzes stability, thresholds, and bifurcations.
result: Beyond a critical adoption threshold, runaway dynamics emerge, causing rapid shifts toward persistent LLM dependence and cognitive competence decline; conversely, reducing transmission or enhancing reversibility can prevent or mitigate such lock-in.
conclusion: LLM adoption is characterized by nonlinear collective dynamics that could erode cognitive autonomy, but proactive measures may offer cognitive immunization against unwanted dependence.

title: In Defence Of The Ehrenfest Mean-field Molecular Dynamics
authors: Vladimir U. Nazarov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Re-visiting the problem of the coupled electronic--nuclear motion, we prove that the so called `mean-field' Ehrenfest picture is an exact theory, rather than an approximation, in the classical limit for nuclei. By establishing its full equivalence to the much more involved Exact Factorization approach to the problem (Abedi {\it et al.}, Europhys. Lett. {\bf 106}, 33001 (2014)), our conclusion rehabilitates the mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics as a simple, effective, while formally exact scheme, amenable to the use within the framework of the time-dependent density functional theory.
tldr: This paper proves that the mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics is exact in the classical limit for nuclei by showing its equivalence to the Exact Factorization approach.
motivation: To rehabilitate the mean-field Ehrenfest method as a formally exact theory rather than an approximation, giving it a solid theoretical foundation for use in time-dependent density functional theory.
method: The author provides a formal proof establishing the full equivalence between the mean-field Ehrenfest picture and the Exact Factorization framework in the classical limit for nuclear motion.
result: The result demonstrates that the mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics is not an approximation but an exact theory under the specified classical-nuclei limit, with direct equivalence to the more involved Exact Factorization scheme.
conclusion: The mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics is a simple, effective, and formally exact scheme, suitable for use within time-dependent density functional theory for electron-nuclear dynamics.

title: Controllability, Returning Waves And Scattering Without Reverberation In 3d Acoustic Dynamic System
authors: Aleksei F. Vakulenko Mikhail I. Belishev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamic acoustic scattering system is governed by the wave equation [MATH] in [MATH], with a compactly supported potential [MATH] and infinitely distant sources (controls) [MATH], which initiate incoming spherical waves [MATH] provided [MATH]. These waves are focused at [MATH] and fill up the whole space at the moment [MATH]. The system is {\it controllable} if the set of waves [MATH] produced by all finite energy controls [MATH], covers the space [MATH]. As we show, if the Hamiltonian [MATH] has the bound states, then in the space the points [MATH] appear such that the system, being refocused at [MATH], loses controllability. The latter leads to a physical effect: the waves [MATH] of finite energy appear, which vanish simultaneously in the past and future cones [MATH] and leave the region of inhomogeneity of [MATH] without reverberation. This effect has some similarities with the wavefront reversal (Time Reversing Mirror), but is more meaningful from a mathematical point of view.
tldr: This paper studies controllability and scattering in a 3D acoustic system with a potential, showing that bound states cause loss of controllability and the emergence of waves without reverberation.
motivation: To understand controllability of acoustic wave systems and the effects of bound states on wave propagation.
method: Mathematical analysis of the wave equation with a compactly supported potential, defining incoming spherical waves and examining controllability of the generated waves.
result: It proves that if the Hamiltonian has bound states, there exist points where the system loses controllability, and finite-energy waves form that vanish in both past and future cones without leaving the inhomogeneity region, thus no reverberation.
conclusion: The described effect is more mathematically significant than related phenomena like time reversal mirrors.

title: Direct Satellite-to-Device Communications: From Cooperative Task Offloading To Non-Cooperative Access Monitoring
authors: Sai Huang, Wanli Ni, Ke Lv, Pengcheng Zhang, Yurui Zheng, Menghan Zhang, Zihui Gong, Zhiyong Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.02955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct satellite-to-device (DS2D) communication is emerging as a transformative paradigm for extending ubiquitous connectivity and edge computing capabilities to remote and underserved regions within 6G non-terrestrial networks. However, practical deployment faces dual critical challenges: i) dynamic satellite channel conditions (e.g., severe Doppler shifts, fast fading) and constrained satellite computing resources in cooperative scenarios; and ii) unauthorized satellite access introduces significant spectrum security threats in non-cooperative scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a versatile DS2D system that supports cooperative task offloading and non-cooperative access monitoring. For cooperative DS2D communications, we integrate a channel estimation module with a dueling double deep Q-network (D3QN) to dynamically optimize task offloading strategy. For non-cooperative DS2D communications, we propose Transformer-based models to enable blind signal detection and automatic modulation classification (AMC). Simulation results show that: 1) The D3QN algorithm reduces average latency by up to 225\% compared to static association policies. 2) Our signal detection model achieves an average presence detection probability of 90.5\% for DS2D signals. 3) The proposed AMC algorithm achieves superior performance across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), with a 9.4\% accuracy gain in low-SNR regimes compared to existing methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a versatile DS2D communication system using D3QN for cooperative task offloading and Transformer-based models for non-cooperative signal detection and modulation classification in 6G non-terrestrial networks.
motivation: The work addresses challenges of dynamic satellite channel conditions and unauthorized access in DS2D communications.
method: It integrates a channel estimation module with a dueling double deep Q-network (D3QN) for task offloading, and uses Transformer-based models for blind signal detection and automatic modulation classification.
result: Simulations show D3QN reduces latency by up to 225%, signal detection achieves 90.5% presence detection probability, and the AMC algorithm gains 9.4% accuracy at low SNR.
conclusion: The proposed DS2D system effectively handles both cooperative and non-cooperative scenarios, demonstrating significant performance improvements.

title: Buckling Prediction For Nonlinear Elastic Beams With Soft Inclusions
authors: Thien Tran-Duc, J. E. Bunder, A. J. Roberts
abstract: ArXiv:2609.02956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an efficient and accurate multiscale computational framework for predicting the buckling and post-buckling behaviour of elastic beams containing periodically distributed soft inclusions. The framework extends our previous multiscale, patch, computational homogenisation for linear elasticity by incorporating nonlinearity, and thus enables accurate prediction of both the buckling onset and the subsequent post-buckling response. Microscale computations are performed only within a sparse set of small subdomains (patches), while the macroscale behaviour is recovered through a proven patch-coupling algorithm. The scheme is assessed through quarter- and half-domain patch computations for beams with inclusion-to-matrix Young's modulus ratios ranging from 0.001 to 1. The results show that reducing the inclusion stiffness lowers both the critical buckling strain and the critical buckling stress, indicating an increased susceptibility to instability, while producing a milder post-buckling response with smaller transverse deflections and stress drops. Eigenvalue analysis of the Jacobian matrix accurately predicts the onset of instability and the corresponding critical strain and stress. Bifurcation diagrams of the nonlinear buckled configurations under compressive loading, and a quantitative analysis of the effect of the interpolation order on the predicted buckling and post-buckling responses, are also presented. Comparisons with full-domain simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately predicts both the buckling threshold and the post-buckling behaviour while substantially reducing the computational cost. The methodology is readily extendable to heterogeneous beams, plates, shells, and other engineering structures.
tldr: This paper presents a multiscale computational framework for predicting buckling in elastic beams with soft inclusions, which is unrelated to quantum information or quantum technologies.
motivation: The user's research interests are exclusively in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems; this paper addresses classical structural mechanics.
method: The authors extend a patch-based computational homogenisation to nonlinear elasticity and perform eigenvalue analysis to predict buckling onset.
result: They show that softer inclusions reduce critical buckling strain/stress and affect post-buckling response.
conclusion: The framework is efficient for heterogeneous structures but has no relevance to quantum research.

title: Variants Of Order Semicontinuity In Banach Lattices
authors: Eugene Bilokopytov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we consider various properties of a normed lattice, which are similar to semicontinuity (also known as the Fatou property), establish relations between these properties, and discuss stability of these properties under renorming. In particular, we show that a normed lattice [MATH] is order continuous iff every renorming of [MATH] is semicontinuous. We also prove that the weakly Fatou (we propose the term ``demicontinuous'') normed lattices are precisely the ones isomorphic to regular sublattices of monotonically complete Banach lattices. In order to do so we introduce the concept of the Lorentz completion of a demicontinuous normed lattice, which is somewhat analogous to the universal completion from the vector lattice theory. Furthermore, we unify and simplify the proofs of the characterizations of monotone completeness from and and provide their quantitative versions. The semicontinuity-related properties in AM-spaces have some additional features. While the classical Kakutani theorem states that AM-spaces are precisely the closed sublattices of [MATH]-spaces, we show, using two different methods, that the semicontinuous AM-spaces are precisely the closed regular sublattices of [MATH]-spaces. Finally, we prove that for a normed space [MATH], the AM-space of positively homogeneous weak* continuous functions on [MATH] is semicontinuous iff it is a regular sublattice of [MATH] iff [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices, establishing relationships and stability under renorming.
motivation: To clarify and unify various semicontinuity-like properties in normed lattices and their characterizations.
method: The paper introduces concepts like Lorentz completion and provides proofs for characterizations of monotone completeness, including quantitative versions.
result: It shows a normed lattice is order continuous iff every renorming is semicontinuous, and characterizes weakly Fatou spaces via regular sublattices.
conclusion: The work generalizes classical results such as Kakutani's theorem to semicontinuous AM-spaces, with applications in functional analysis.

title: Structural Compatibility And Uniform Stability Of Temporally Degenerate Parabolic Systems
authors: Amadou Ciss\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern feedback design for distributed parameter systems presupposes that the closed-loop dynamics define a well-posed evolution problem. This presupposition becomes nontrivial for temporally degenerate parabolic systems, where temporal degeneracy affects not only the analytical properties of the evolution equation but also the mathematical formulation of the feedback interconnection itself. It is shown that admissible feedback interconnections for temporally degenerate parabolic systems are completely characterized by an operator compatibility condition linking the singular reaction operator with the actuator and observation operators. This characterization removes the singular component of the closed-loop dynamics and reduces the degenerate evolution equation to a regular evolution equation. Building upon this regularized formulation, a critical--residual decomposition yields a uniform exponential stability certificate, which is subsequently extended to the original infinite-dimensional evolution through a finite-to-infinite lifting theorem. A constructive static output feedback synthesis is finally obtained as a consequence of these results. Numerical experiments illustrate the regularization mechanism, validate the stability certificate, and confirm the finite-to-infinite lifting.
tldr: This paper characterizes admissible feedback interconnections for temporally degenerate parabolic systems via an operator compatibility condition, enabling regularization and uniform exponential stability certification.
motivation: Feedback design for distributed parameter systems presupposes well-posedness, which becomes nontrivial for temporally degenerate parabolic systems where degeneracy affects both analytical properties and feedback formulation.
method: The authors introduce an operator compatibility condition linking the singular reaction operator with actuator and observation operators, remove the singular component to obtain a regular evolution equation, and use a critical–residual decomposition to derive stability certificates extended via a finite-to-infinite lifting theorem.
result: A uniform exponential stability certificate is obtained and extended to the original infinite-dimensional evolution, yielding a constructive static output feedback synthesis.
conclusion: Numerical experiments validate the regularization mechanism, stability certificate, and finite-to-infinite lifting, confirming the theoretical findings.

title: Coupled Tensor-Tensor Completion Method With Applications In Drug Repurposing
authors: Maryam Bagherian, Albert Hung, Ivo Dinov, Joshua Welch
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many biomedical challenges can be posed as tensor completion problems where the observed entries of a multidimensional array (a tensor) are used to impute the missing values. In such settings, incorporating side information about the modes of the tensor, such as gene-gene similarity, can significantly enhance the solutions of the completion problem. Most existing tensor completion methods can only incorporate side information in the form of matrices. In this study, we introduce a novel framework to incorporate side information in the form of tensors. Our new approach, called Coupled Tensor-Tensor Completion (CTTC), leverages the hidden connections among multimodal tensors to improve tensor completion performance. In addition to practical utility, CTTC has theoretical foundations in distance metric learning and group theory. We derive an alternating algorithm to solve the CTTC optimization problem and establish its convergence to a stationary point. Finally, we show that CTTC outperforms state-of-the-art tensor completion methods at predicting drug effects. Results: Compared with other tensor completion methods, including HaLRTC, CTRC, Cell, and NTDDR, CTTC demonstrates superior run-time and RSE tensor completion accuracy on two benchmark datasets, DTD and LINCS.
tldr: Introduces a coupled tensor-tensor completion method that incorporates tensor side information to improve drug repurposing predictions.
motivation: Existing tensor completion methods only use matrix side information, which limits performance; this work aims to leverage tensor side information to enhance drug effect prediction.
method: Proposes the Coupled Tensor-Tensor Completion (CTTC) framework, which uses hidden connections among multimodal tensors and provides an alternating algorithm with convergence guarantees.
result: CTTC outperforms state-of-the-art tensor completion methods (e.g., HaLRTC, CTRC) on drug effect prediction benchmarks (DTD and LINCS) in terms of run-time and accuracy.
conclusion: Incorporating tensor side information via CTTC improves tensor completion for drug repurposing, offering a promising tool for biomedical data analysis.

title: Stability Of Maximal Relative Projection Constants
authors: Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar, Seyed Ahmad Mojallal, Shivaramakrishna Pragada

It is known that for any fixed [MATH], [MATH] is a non-decreasing sequence with limit [MATH] as [MATH]. A natural question is whether [MATH] stabilizes at [MATH] for some [MATH]. We prove that for any fixed [MATH], \[\lambda(r,n)=\lambda(r) \qquad \qquad n\ge 2^{r}{2}.\] This answers a question of Basso. The technique used is of independent interest.

motivation: To determine whether the sequence of maximal relative projection constants stabilizes at some finite n for each fixed r.
method: The authors develop a novel mathematical technique, claimed to be of independent interest, to establish the stability result.
result: It is shown that λ(r,n)=λ(r) for all n ≥ 2^{r}2, confirming stabilization.
conclusion: The open question posed by Basso is answered, and the method may have broader applications in functional analysis.

title: Adaptive Beam Hopping And Power Control For Dual-Layer Over-the-Air Online Federated Learning In Leo Satellite Networks
authors: Zhendong Li, Shaojie Wang, Zhou Su, Zihao Zhang, Haixia Peng, Nan Cheng, Ying Wang, Wen Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air (OTA) computation enabled online federated learning (FL) in low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Specifically, we consider a dual-layer OTA aggregation architecture, where ground devices upload analog model updates to serving satellites via uplink OTA aggregation, and satellites forward the aggregated signals to a data processing center through the second round OTA aggregation. Then, we formulate a long-term data-utilization maximization problem in which devices continuously collect new data and untrained samples gradually lose freshness. The problem is subject to the satellite beam budget, transmit-power limit, and global mean squared error (MSE) constraint that governs end-to-end aggregation distortion. This yields a coupled mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, involving tightly coupled discrete beam-hopping decisions and continuous power control. Due to the combinatorial action space and nonconvex constraints, the problem is NP-hard and computationally intractable. Furthermore, the time-varying satellite topology and dynamic data generation render it a sequential decision-making problem, necessitating adaptive online scheduling. To address these issues, we cast the problem as a Markov decision process and develop a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes adaptive beam hopping and power control, using an MSE-aware reward to balance data utilization and aggregation accuracy. Numerical simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms other benchmark schemes, achieving superior long-term data utilization and faster FL convergence while satisfying the MSE requirement.
tldr: This paper addresses adaptive beam hopping and power control for over-the-air federated learning in LEO satellite networks using deep reinforcement learning, which is entirely outside quantum information science.
motivation: The paper aims to optimize data utilization and convergence in a dual-layer over-the-air aggregation architecture for online federated learning over LEO satellites, a practical communication and machine learning problem.
method: It formulates a mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem with discrete beam-hopping and continuous power control, models it as a Markov decision process, and solves it with a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework that uses an MSE-aware reward.
result: Numerical simulations show the proposed algorithm outperforms benchmarks in long-term data utilization and FL convergence while meeting the mean squared error constraint.
conclusion: The contribution is relevant to satellite communications and federated learning optimization, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Novel Parallel Approach For Solving Some Free Boundary Value Problems
authors: Amboru Yalmanda Peeyush Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a novel, efficient class of parallel direct and indirect iterative schemes to solve general obstacle and free boundary value problems. The uniqueness of the solution for the direct parallel method is established under the assumption that the model problem yields an [MATH]-matrix. The convergence analysis of the indirect approach is predicated on minimizing the discrete energy functional at each iterative stage of the linear approximation process. Under the aforementioned setting, we establish theoretical convergence results for both smooth and nonsmooth energy functionals defined over a convex set, in the sense of Ferris and Mangasarian . For the numerical computation of the one-dimensional obstacle problem, we adopt a direct generalized parallel approach based on the SPIKE algorithm . To accelerate convergence and reduce computational complexity, a fast recursive version of the scheme is generalized to the nonsmooth case. For two- and three-dimensional obstacle problems, we employ a directional splitting method that treats each directional subproblem as a one-dimensional obstacle minimization problem. By framing the energy functional minimization as a parabolic time-dependent problem and utilizing an Armijo time-stepping rule during the solution update process, we successfully obtain results for higher-dimensional obstacles. Additionally, this study explores the possibility of extending the algorithm into a constrained quadratic programming optimization solver. We also evaluate the framework on image deblurring phenomena under the aforementioned setting, successfully recovering the original images. Finally, numerical illustrations are provided to validate the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper proposes parallel numerical methods for solving obstacle and free boundary value problems, with applications to image deblurring.
motivation: To develop efficient parallel algorithms for solving obstacle-type free boundary problems, which arise in many applications like image processing and contact mechanics.
method: The study introduces direct and indirect iterative schemes, including a generalized SPIKE algorithm for 1D problems and directional splitting for higher dimensions, with an Armijo time-stepping rule for energy minimization.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the methods for 1D, 2D, and 3D obstacle problems and image deblurring, with convergence validated.
conclusion: The proposed parallel approach is efficient and viable for solving free boundary value problems, though it is completely unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: An Exact Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound Algorithm For The Job Sequencing And Tool Switching Problem
authors: Alberto Locatelli, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois C\^ot\'e, Leandro C. Coelho
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem (SSP) is a well-known combinatorial optimization problem arising in the context of flexible manufacturing. Since the seminal work of Tang and Denardo (1988), the SSP has received significant attention in the literature, leading to the development of numerous exact and heuristic approaches. Despite these efforts, several benchmark instances proposed decades ago and containing only 20 jobs have remained unsolved to proven optimality. In this work, we propose an exact algorithm for the SSP, namely the Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound (C-B\&B) algorithm, which combines two distinct branch-and-bound algorithms, each introducing novel features compared with the existing literature. The former relies on a new branching scheme designed to reduce the size of the implicit enumeration tree, together with a collection of new bounding functions. The latter builds on the branching scheme introduced by Laporte et al. (2004) and strengthens it with a new bounding function and two dominance rules. Within C-B\&B, these exact algorithms are complemented by a preprocessing phase that incorporates a new branch-and-bound-based heuristic capable of rapidly generating a high-quality initial incumbent solution. Extensive computational experiments show that C-B\&B represents a strong breakthrough over previously published approaches, proving optimality for more instances with significantly less computational effort and closing several benchmark instances that have remained open for decades.
tags: Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem
tldr: This paper proposes an exact Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound algorithm for the Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem, solving benchmark instances that have been open for decades.
motivation: The SSP is a classical combinatorial optimization problem in manufacturing, and despite numerous algorithms, several small benchmark instances remain unsolved, motivating the need for a more effective exact method.
method: The C-B&B algorithm combines two branch-and-bound algorithms with novel branching schemes and bounding functions, complemented by a preprocessing heuristic to generate a good initial solution.
result: Extensive experiments show that C-B&B proves optimality for more instances with significantly less computational effort, closing several open benchmark instances.
conclusion: The proposed exact algorithm marks a strong improvement over previous approaches for the SSP, demonstrating that even decades-old instances can now be solved efficiently.
keywords: Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem

title: Weighted Ces\`aro Type Operators On The Weighted Bergman Spaces In The Unit Ball
authors: Jiaxin Pan, Cezhong Tong, Zicong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study weighted Ces\`aro type operators \[ \mathcal C_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}:A_{\alpha}^{p}(\mathbb B_n) \longrightarrow A_{\alpha}^{q}(\mathbb B_n) \] induced by measures on [MATH], and obtain boundedness characterizations throughout the range [MATH]. By means of atomic decomposition, we further treat the case [MATH] and [MATH], thereby obtaining a complete characterization for [MATH]. The latter result is new even in one dimension. For the range [MATH], we characterize the boundedness in terms of an integral condition involving the tail function of the inducing measure. This result is also new even on the unit disk. Finally, we characterize the boundedness of the corresponding operators when the target space is [MATH].
tldr: This paper focuses on boundedness characterizations of weighted Cesàro type operators acting between weighted Bergman spaces on the unit ball, a topic in classical function theory and operator theory.
motivation: To establish clear criteria for when these integral operators are bounded between different Bergman spaces, a fundamental question in complex analysis and operator theory.
method: The authors employ atomic decomposition techniques and introduce integral conditions involving tail functions to derive the boundedness characterizations across various parameter ranges.
result: They obtain complete characterizations for the boundedness of the operators for certain parameter ranges, with results that are new even in one-dimensional cases, and also treat cases that require integral conditions.
conclusion: The paper contributes new mathematical theorems about Cesàro type operators on Bergman spaces, but it is entirely unrelated to the specified research interests in quantum information and related areas.

title: A Joint Power-Privacy Control Framework For Decentralized Learning Over Heterogeneous Wireless Multicasting Networks
authors: Amir Ziaeddini, Yauhen Yakimenka, Joerg Kliewer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a decentralized learning framework that incorporates both power control and privacy guarantees. Specifically, we enable a set of clients in a wireless multicast network to jointly train a common model while maintaining a prescribed per-iteration maximum privacy leakage level. The communication network is represented by a rowstochastic adjacency matrix, allowing us to capture asymmetric channel gains as well as heterogeneous maximum transmit power levels. Differential privacy is enforced through an explicit powersplitting strategy that allocates each node's limited maximum transmit power between model coefficients and injected Gaussian noise, thereby jointly controlling learning performance and privacy leakage. We further prove that the proposed algorithm achieves a cumulative regret bound of O(logT), whereTdenotes the time horizon. To evaluate the practical performance of our approach, we perform comprehensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset under both IID and non-IID data distributions, considering different privacy levels, diverse numbers of clients, and various graph topologies. The results demonstrate strong performance across the considered settings and improved performance over existing methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm under realistic wireless communication constraints.
tldr: This paper proposes a decentralized learning framework that jointly optimizes power control and differential privacy over wireless multicast networks, achieving a regret bound of O(log T).
motivation: To address the challenges of decentralized learning under realistic wireless constraints, including limited transmit power and privacy requirements.
method: It employs a row-stochastic adjacency matrix to model asymmetric channels and a power-splitting strategy to allocate power between model coefficients and Gaussian noise for differential privacy.
result: Experiments on CIFAR-10, under IID and non-IID data, various privacy levels, and network topologies, demonstrate strong performance and improvements over existing methods.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical solution for privacy-preserving decentralized learning in wireless multicast settings, balancing accuracy and privacy.

title: Accelerated Prox-Level Methods For Unknown Piecewise-Smooth Optimization Ii: Function-constrained Optimization
authors: Zhe Zhang Zhenewei Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an anytime, almost parameter-free algorithm for convex function-constrained optimization, in which the objective and constraint functions are unknown piecewise-smooth. Our algorithm, Restarted Penalty APEX (Penalty Accelerated Prox-level method for Exploring Piecewise Smoothness), is an accelerated bundle-level method based on the penalty approach. For problems satisfying quadratic growth, the proposed method is the first to achieve optimal oracle complexity without knowing the growth modulus or the exact penalty coefficient. Furthermore, Restarted Penalty APEX generates a verifiable certificate that bounds both the optimality gap and the constraint violation. This certificate also appears to be new to the literature.
tldr: This paper introduces an accelerated penalty-based method for convex function-constrained optimization with unknown piecewise-smooth functions, achieving optimal oracle complexity and providing verifiable certificates.
motivation: To solve convex function-constrained optimization problems where the objective and constraint functions are unknown piecewise-smooth, without requiring knowledge of growth parameters.
method: The proposed Restarted Penalty APEX algorithm is accelerated bundle-level method based on a penalty approach, designed to be anytime and almost parameter-free.
result: It is the first method to achieve optimal oracle complexity for quadratic growth problems without knowing the growth modulus or exact penalty coefficient, and it generates a certificate bounding optimality gap and constraint violation.
conclusion: The work advances optimization theory, but it is unrelated to the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Trapping Of Ray Families By Mirrors
authors: Casey O'malley
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We settle two questions of Serge Tabachnikov regarding the trapping of light rays by mirrors. We show (i) that the largest dimension of a trapped family of rays in [MATH] is [MATH], and (ii) that in [MATH] one can trap a 2-parameter family of rays that is not locally normal to any smooth surface. We first establish that no [MATH]-parameter family can be trapped by showing that no open subset of [MATH] can be trapped due to Poincar\'e's recurrence theorem, yielding an upper bound of [MATH]. We then show that a system of mirrors traps a [MATH] parameter family of rays by noting that a compact subset of the set of states of rays in the central "waist" of the trap is a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold, making it amenable to a stable manifold theorem for NHIMs, which implies that the set of rays asymptotic to the waist of the trap has dimension [MATH]. We then truncate our mirror system, which permits the entrance of rays from arbitrarily far outside of the trap, attaining the upper bound [MATH] and resolving the first question. We then show that in [MATH], there exists within the trapped family of rays a 2-parameter subfamily on which the canonical symplectic form on the space of oriented lines is nowhere vanishing, implying that the subfamily is not locally normal to any smooth surface, which settles the second question.
tldr: This paper proves results about the maximal dimension of trapped families of light rays by mirrors, resolving two open questions posed by Serge Tabachnikov.
motivation: The work addresses open problems in geometric optics and billiard theory regarding the possibility of trapping families of rays with mirrors.
method: The proof uses Poincaré's recurrence theorem to establish upper bounds, and employs the theory of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds and their stable manifolds to construct trapped families; additionally, symplectic geometry is applied to analyze the local normal property.
result: It is shown that no open set of rays can be trapped in a certain setting, while a maximal-dimensional trapped family exists, and in a specific case a 2-parameter family is constructed that is not locally normal to any smooth surface.
conclusion: The questions about ray trapping are fully answered, contributing to the mathematical understanding of billiards and ray dynamics.

title: Mean-field Optimal Stopping With Endogenous Quantile Cutoffs
authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Ibrahim Ekren, Xihao He
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a mean-field optimal stopping problem with an endogenous population-level shutdown. All remaining agents stop when the survival mass falls below a prescribed threshold. We recast the discontinuous objective as the singular, nonconvex constraint that the survival mass lie in [MATH]. We prove the equivalence of strong and weak values via an approximation and the existence of an optimal rule via compactness and penalization. We also prove a dynamic programming principle. The value is continuous away from the critical boundary but may be discontinuous at the boundary itself. Under strict initial feasibility, finite-population values converge to the mean-field value. In the same regime, the laws of near-optimal empirical measures are tight and every mean-field optimizer admits a recovery sequence. At the threshold, however, finite-population convergence may fail.
tldr: This paper studies a mean-field optimal stopping problem with an endogenous quantile cutoff, analyzing value continuity and finite-population convergence.
motivation: To understand optimal stopping when the population stops once the mass falls below a threshold, which arises in systemic risk and cascading failures.
method: Proves equivalence of strong and weak values via approximation, proves existence via compactness and penalization, and establishes a dynamic programming principle.
result: Shows continuity away from the critical boundary, potential discontinuity at the boundary, and finite-population convergence under strict feasibility, with possible failure at the threshold.
conclusion: Provides a framework for analyzing mean-field optimal stopping with endogenous cutoffs, highlighting boundary effects.

title: Method Of Successive Approximations For Solving Integral Equations Of Actuarial Mathematics
authors: Bogdan Norkin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dissertation considers various generalizations of the classical risk process describing the stochastic evolution of the capital of an insurance company (Cramer Lundberg model), including processes with variable deterministic or random premiums, non Poisson flows of premiums and claims, and a stochastic Markovian environment. Integral equations for the probability of nonruin as a function of initial capital are derived for these generalizations. For processes in a stochastic Markovian environment, systems of integral equations for nonruin probabilities corresponding to different initial states are obtained. General necessary and sufficient, as well as specific sufficient, conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions are established. A successive approximation method for numerical and analytical solution of the integral equations is theoretically and practically validated; its uniform convergence and rate of convergence are established. A technique for estimating the accuracy of approximate solutions is developed by constructing upper and lower approximations to the exact solution. The method is tested on numerical examples and compared with the Monte Carlo method and known solution approximations. The developed method increases the accuracy of actuarial calculations: it allows the probability of ruin to be calculated with any prescribed accuracy, empirical approximations to be verified and improved iteratively, and the accuracy and parameters of Monte Carlo simulations to be estimated and corrected.
tldr: This paper introduces a successive approximation method to solve integral equations for ruin probabilities in generalized insurance risk processes, improving numerical accuracy in actuarial calculations.
motivation: To accurately compute nonruin probabilities for various insurance risk models, including those with Markovian environments and non-Poisson claim flows, which lack analytical solutions.
method: The author derives integral equations and systems thereof for nonruin probabilities, establishes existence/uniqueness conditions, and develops a successive approximation algorithm with rigorous convergence and error bounds using upper/lower approximations.
result: The method achieves any prescribed accuracy, is validated on numerical examples, and compares favorably with Monte Carlo simulations and existing approximations.
conclusion: The proposed technique enhances actuarial risk assessment by enabling precise ruin probability calculations and iterative refinement of empirical estimates.

title: A Unified Theory Of H-Duality In First-Order Methods
authors: Alex L. Wang Kevin Shu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide two complementary explanations of H-duality in smooth strongly convex optimization and contractive fixed-point problems. H-duality refers to the phenomenon where the worst-case performance of many fixed-step first-order methods (FSFOMs) for a given performance setup are exactly equal to the worst-case performance of their "time-reversed" counterparts and a paired performance setup. This concept gained interest as a mechanism for automatically converting an algorithm with guarantees on the final suboptimality to algorithms with guarantees on the final gradient norm. Since its initial discovery, additional H-dual performance setup pairings have been discovered empirically, yet a general explanation for these phenomena remained elusive. Our first explanation of H-duality shows that, on a class of instances with extremal curvature properties, FSFOMs produce a final iterate that is a scalar multiple of the initial iterate, and that this scalar is invariant under the time reversal of the underlying FSFOM. This, together with the empirical observation that many FSFOMs have such an instance with extremal curvature as their worst case, gives one explanation for why H-duality often occurs. The second explanation is complementary and uses the notion of a performance estimation certificate of the convergence rate of a FSFOM. We exhibit an explicit transformation of such certificates that preserves many of the properties that define such a certificate, and we show that in many numerical and analytical examples, this transformation in fact transforms certificates of the convergence rate of an algorithm into certificates for its time-reversal. As an application, we prove a convergence guarantee for the H-dual of ITEM matching the conjectured optimal gradient-to-gradient guarantee.
tldr: This paper provides a unified theory of H-duality in smooth strongly convex optimization and contractive fixed-point problems, explaining why certain first-order methods and their time-reversed counterparts have matching worst-case performance.
motivation: H-duality is an empirical phenomenon in optimization lacking a general theoretical explanation; the authors aim to provide rigorous justifications.
method: The authors present two complementary explanations: one based on extremal-curvature instances where iterates scale invariance under time reversal, and another using performance estimation certificates (PECs) with an explicit transformation preserving certificate properties.
result: They prove a convergence guarantee for the H-dual of ITEM that matches the conjectured optimal gradient-to-gradient guarantee, demonstrating the practical utility of their framework.
conclusion: The paper establishes a theoretical foundation for H-duality, potentially enabling automated conversion of optimization algorithms between different performance metrics.

title: Geometric Ergodicity Of Affine Invariant Ensemble Langevin And Its Discrete Time Variants
authors: Yifan Chen Hong Ye Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Affine-invariant ensemble samplers are widely used in Bayesian applications. However, their quantitative convergence theory, in particular geometric ergodicity, remains a basic open question. We study the affine invariant ensemble Langevin dynamics, an interacting particle system that uses the empirical covariance of the whole ensemble as a preconditioner. While effective in practice, theoretical understanding of this method is not available beyond plain qualitative convergence in total variation; a central difficulty is that the empirical covariance can approach singularity. This paper addresses this challenge. For potentials with bounded Hessian that are strongly convex outside a ball, we prove geometric ergodicity using a novel Lyapunov function that combines an inverse-covariance barrier with a coercive exponential energy. We then show that directly applying the Euler--Maruyama scheme can diverge with positive probability, even for a one-dimensional Gaussian target. This motivates a covariance-trace time regularization. We prove geometric ergodicity of the regularized diffusion and, for sufficiently small step size, of its unadjusted Euler--Maruyama discretization. We also show that the invariant distributions of the discretization converge weakly to the product target distribution as the step size tends to zero.
tldr: This paper proves geometric ergodicity for affine invariant ensemble Langevin dynamics and its regularized discretizations, addressing a long-standing open question in MCMC theory.
motivation: Affine-invariant ensemble samplers are widely used but lack quantitative convergence theory; specifically geometric ergodicity was an open question due to potential singularity of empirical covariance.
method: The authors introduce a novel Lyapunov function combining an inverse-covariance barrier with a coercive exponential energy to prove geometric ergodicity for potentials with bounded Hessian and strong convexity outside a ball. They also propose a covariance-trace time regularization to avoid divergence in Euler-Maruyama discretizations, and analyze the discretized algorithm's convergence.
result: They prove geometric ergodicity for the continuous-time dynamics and for the regularized diffusion, and establish weak convergence of the invariant measures of the discretization to the product target as step size goes to zero.
conclusion: The paper provides the first quantitative convergence results for affine invariant ensemble Langevin samplers, advancing the theoretical understanding of these widely used methods.

title: Learning Informative Prior With Infinite-Dimensional Continuous Normalizing Flow For Bayesian Inverse Problem
authors: Yang Zhao, Junxiong Jia, Tao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses infinite-dimensional Bayesian inference for inverse problem of partial differential equations with model parameters in infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. To effectively incorporate prior information, we propose a novel continuous normalizing flows based infinite-dimensional model. Specifically, by introducing a well-defined neural ordinary differential equation in infinite-dimensional space, a simple reference measure can be transformed into a more complex measure which encodes the prior information. A corresponding theoretical framework is established to ensure the well-posedness of our proposed Bayesian prior in infinite-dimensional space. We also provide training methods of the prior for two distinct data settings, along with two sampling algorithms for the resulting Bayesian posterior. The proposed framework is applied to three representative inverse problems: the simple smooth inverse problem, inverse scattering problem, and the inverse heat conduction problem. Numerical experiments support the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithms.
tldr: This paper introduces an infinite-dimensional continuous normalizing flow method to learn informative priors for Bayesian inverse problems of PDEs.
motivation: Bayesian inverse problems for PDEs require effective incorporation of prior information in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, which is challenging with existing methods.
method: The authors propose a neural ODE in infinite-dimensional space to transform a simple reference measure into a complex prior measure, establish theoretical well-posedness, and provide training and sampling algorithms.
result: Numerical experiments on smooth, inverse scattering, and inverse heat conduction problems demonstrate the efficiency and support the theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a principled and effective approach for learning informative priors in infinite-dimensional Bayesian inverse problems.

title: Hyperpositive Functions, Sector Bounded Functions And A Trace Formula
authors: Izchak Lewkowicz Daniel Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an indexed family of functions closely related to functions ana- lytic and with a real positive part in the right open half plane (the so-called positive functions) and to the functions analytic in the right open half-plane and bounded in modulus by one there (the so-called bounded functions). These two families are related by the Cayley transform. In the present paper we introduce an affine linear relation- ship between a subclass of positive functions and the family of bounded functions, and study the corresponding connections with passivity of linear systems, interpolation and operator models. This is therefore a multidisciplinary paper, with potential readers from engineering, linear system theory and operator theory, and some repetitions of known results are given to allow various audiences to read the work. Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of analytic functions are a key tool in the arguments. A special role is played by the de Branges-Rovnyak spaces associated to bounded functions, and we prove a related trace formula connecting an underlying pair of operators.
tldr: The paper introduces an affine linear relationship between a subclass of positive functions and bounded functions, connecting to passivity of linear systems and proving a trace formula using de Branges-Rovnyak spaces.
motivation: The work aims to study connections between positive and bounded analytic functions via an affine transformation, with applications in linear system theory and operator theory.
method: The authors introduce an indexed family of functions, use the Cayley transform, and employ reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and de Branges-Rovnyak spaces to derive the trace formula.
result: Establishes an affine relationship and proves a trace formula linking an underlying pair of operators, with interdisciplinary relevance.
conclusion: The paper is multidisciplinary, targeting readers from engineering, linear system theory, and operator theory.

title: Sampling And Density Theorems For The Fractional Opdam-Cherednik Transform
authors: Anirudha Poria Riya Ghosh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish sampling and density results for the fractional Opdam-Cherednik transform. Using the Sturm-Liouville structure of Jacobi functions, we construct a Riesz basis associated with the Opdam-Cherednik kernel and derive an explicit sampling formula. The sampling nodes are determined by the zeros of a shifted Jacobi function. We further develop a concentration-operator approach and obtain Landau-type necessary density conditions for sampling and interpolation in fractional Opdam-Cherednik bandlimited spaces. The non-fractional Opdam-Cherednik sampling formula is recovered when [MATH].
tldr: The paper establishes sampling and density theorems for the fractional Opdam-Cherednik transform.
motivation: To extend sampling theory to the fractional Opdam-Cherednik transform and provide necessary conditions for sampling and interpolation.
method: Uses the Sturm-Liouville structure of Jacobi functions to construct a Riesz basis and applies a concentration-operator approach.
result: Derives an explicit sampling formula and Landau-type necessary density conditions.
conclusion: Provides sampling and interpolation results for fractional bandlimited spaces, recovering the non-fractional case as a special case.

title: Almost-invariant Half-spaces Of Operators On $\omega$
authors: No\'emie Fougnies
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Almost-Invariant Subspace Problem for operators defined on non-normable Fr\'echet spaces and especially on [MATH]. This problem is stated as follows: "Given a bounded operator [MATH] on an infinite-dimensional complex Fr\'echet space [MATH], can we always find a closed almost-invariant half-space?". In this paper we solve the problem for the space [MATH] by showing that an operator [MATH] on [MATH] possesses a closed almost-invariant half-space if and only if [MATH] is conjugate to [MATH] or to [MATH] where [MATH] is the Forward shift and [MATH] is the Backward shift and where [MATH] is a finite rank operator and [MATH]. We also investigate the case of operators defined on [MATH] where [MATH] is an infinite-dimensional Fr\'echet space with a continuous norm and we show that in this case, every operator defined on [MATH] possesses a closed almost-invariant half-space.
tldr: This paper studies almost-invariant half-spaces for operators on non-normable Fréchet spaces, particularly the space ω, solving the problem under certain conditions.
motivation: The work addresses the Almost-Invariant Subspace Problem in infinite-dimensional functional analysis, seeking to generalize results from Banach spaces to Fréchet spaces.
method: The author analyzes the existence of closed almost-invariant half-spaces for operators on ω and other Fréchet spaces with continuous norms, characterizing when such subspaces exist and investigating conjugacy to shift operators.
result: For the space ω, it is shown that an operator possesses a closed almost-invariant half-space if and only if it is conjugate to a forward or backward shift plus a finite-rank operator. For any infinite-dimensional Fréchet space with a continuous norm, every operator has such a half-space.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete solution to the problem on ω and extends the existence result to a broader class of Fréchet spaces, contributing to operator theory but not to the user's research areas.

title: On The Complexity Of Recognizing Sdp Exactness For The Maximum Cut Problem
authors: Avinash Bhardwaj
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxation of the Maximum Cut (Max-Cut) problem is exact when its optimal value equals the integer maximum cut, geometrically corresponding to a rank-1 optimal solution. While the pioneering work of Delorme and Poljak established that recognizing exactness is NP-hard, their reduction relied on exponentially scaling edge weights. This established only weak NP-hardness and explicitly left open the complexity for simple, unweighted graphs. In this paper, we resolve the computational complexity of the exactness property. First, we prove that deciding SDP exactness for weighted graphs is strongly NP-hard by constructing a sum-of-squares dual certificate with polynomially bounded integer weights. Second, we extend this hardness to simple, unweighted graphs via a geometric embedding of restricted Not-All-Equal 4-SAT into edge-disjoint clique structures. Both proofs utilize geometric locking mechanisms that force the continuous SDP relaxation to an absolute global minimum, decoupling the continuous bounds from the underlying combinatorial hardness.
tldr: This paper resolves the computational complexity of recognizing SDP exactness for the Max-Cut problem, proving strong NP-hardness for weighted and unweighted graphs.
motivation: The SDP relaxation of Max-Cut is exact when its optimal value equals the integer maximum cut, and previously only weak NP-hardness was known due to exponentially scaling edge weights. The authors aim to settle the complexity for simple unweighted graphs.
method: They construct sum-of-squares dual certificates with polynomially bounded integer weights to prove strong NP-hardness for weighted graphs, and extend this to unweighted graphs via geometric embedding of restricted Not-All-Equal 4-SAT into edge-disjoint clique structures.
result: The paper proves that deciding SDP exactness is strongly NP-hard for weighted graphs and also NP-hard for simple, unweighted graphs.
conclusion: The complexity of recognizing SDP exactness for Max-Cut is now fully resolved, with both weighted and unweighted cases shown to be hard.

title: Beyond Higher-Pulse Rectification: Operational Harmonic Coordination In Renewable P2h Systems
authors: Yangjun Zeng (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Yiwei Qiu (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Jie Zhu (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Yi Zhou (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Tao Wu (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Xin Meng (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Shi Chen (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Buxiang Zhou (college Of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University), Kaigui Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thyristor rectifiers (TRs) are cost-effective electrolysis power supplies for renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) systems, but their harmonics may violate grid-code limits. In contrast to conventional solutions that rely on higher-pulse (such as 24-pulse) rectifiers, this paper proposes an operational harmonic coordination scheme that enables low-cost 12-pulse TRs to meet harmonic requirements through coordinated operation. First, a harmonic model quantifies the effects of rectifier transformer (RCT) tap positions and electrolytic currents, enabling harmonic cancellation among multiple electrolyzers (ELZs). A two-layer framework then coordinates hydrogen production and harmonic mitigation. Hourly scheduling determines ELZ commitment within the harmonic feasible region under renewable uncertainty using stochastic programming and a modified progressive hedging algorithm, while minute-level dispatch tracks renewable power and mitigates harmonics. A decomposition algorithm separates production dispatch from harmonic mitigation to improve computational efficiency. Case studies based on real-life projects show that the proposed method increases profit by 31% over current-only regulation. Annual simulations further show that coordinated 12-pulse TRs can replace 24-pulse rectifiers for harmonic compliance by exchanging additional RCT tap actions for lower transformer investment, reducing rectification-stage cost by 37.5%.
tldr: Proposes an operational harmonic coordination scheme for renewable power-to-hydrogen systems using low-cost 12-pulse thyristor rectifiers to meet harmonic requirements.
motivation: Higher-pulse rectifiers are expensive; the goal is to use cheaper 12-pulse rectifiers while complying with grid harmonic limits.
method: A two-layer framework coordinates hydrogen production and harmonic mitigation through hourly scheduling and minute-level dispatch, using stochastic programming and a modified progressive hedging algorithm.
result: The method increases profit by 31% over current-only regulation and allows 12-pulse rectifiers to replace 24-pulse units, reducing rectification-stage cost by 37.5%.
conclusion: Coordinated operation of multiple electrolyzers can achieve harmonic compliance at lower cost.

title: Well-posedness Of Filtering Equations In Weighted Sobolev Spaces With Unbounded System Coefficients
authors: Zeju Sun, Songlin Zhou, Stephen S. -T. Yau
abstract: ArXiv:2609.03549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear filtering problem is one of the core subjects in modern control theory. In this paper, we will study the well-posedness of the three fundamental evolution equations arising in continuous-time nonlinear filtering--the robust Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, the stochastic DMZ equation, and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation--within a unified buffered weighted formulation. An exponential-type weight function and the corresponding weighted Sobolev spaces are introduced to enable a variational treatment of the filtering equations in a more general setting, in which the coefficients of the filtering system may be unbounded with polynomial growth. Under mild and easily verifiable assumptions, we first establish the well-posedness of the weak solution to the robust DMZ equation in these weighted spaces. Using the gauge (exponential) transformation and its inverse, these results are then transferred to the stochastic DMZ equation and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation, whose solutions are shown to exist and be unique in buffered weighted Sobolev spaces, yielding a unified treatment of all three filtering equations. Sufficient conditions for the well-posedness are also summarized, which illustrate the wide applicability of the proposed framework to general nonlinear filtering systems.
